::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 13th [1867]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Library of Congress
:::

My dear [Miss Sewell](people/person_1301.qmd)
My senses have returned for thinking and writing indeed for anything but walking. It seems to me that we might settle a great deal in a June council, [Mary Coleridge](people/person_351.qmd) is to be here for a week at the beginning of the month otherwise we are quite clear. I will send you [Freeman](other_books/otherbook_482.qmd) tomorrow. It seems to me that his first seven pages, with perhaps his 4th chapter abridged would be very useful. I have his leave and [Mr Palgrave](people/person_1124.qmd)’s.[^1] I will have the introduction rewritten by the time you come. I think our critics will be puzzled whose style it is. We shall be very glad indeed to see you when you have time for a séance.

The Simeons have no [Queen Emma](people/person_485.qmd)s left but [Savage](people/person_1283.qmd) may have and I will try there.[^2] Poor [Captain Simeon](people/person_1322.qmd)lingers on but is worse every time we hear of him

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: She had obtained Francis Turner Palgrave's permission to use an extract from his father's *History of Normandy and England* in the book of *Historical Selections* she and Sewell were editing
[^3]: This must mean 'no photographs of Queen Emma'.
